items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: Well I guess, as Ellington said, “There’s good music and bad music.”

ctx.x: He has influenced my wife because my wife used to listen to jazz records. Now I walk in the house and there’s like Luciano Pavarotti on. He gave her the records. It’s constant. I mean I love it you know, but it’s constant and she used to be a jazz freak, you know, loved jazz.
Well I guess, as Ellington said, “There’s good music and bad music.” Did he say that? He said a lot of things. It sounds like something he might have said.
Yeah, I think he did say it, yeah.
